findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate the timing AC as evidence-recording only (record before/after focused serial + exact-xdist elapsed) OR give a concrete baseline and reduction threshold, resolving whether it is a hard gate.
evidence: The AC uses the comparative 'lower' with no stated baseline value or threshold.
Plan step 6 says 'Timing remains evidence only.' — conflicting with listing it as a checkable AC.
findings.finding: The acceptance criterion 'Focused serial plus exact-xdist evidence shows lower elapsed runner work' gives no baseline or magnitude, making 'lower' unmeasurable as a pass/fail gate.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'Focused serial plus exact-xdist evidence shows lower elapsed runner work.'
scenarios: Executor cannot decide whether a marginal or noisy reduction satisfies the criterion.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the AC to 'Focused serial and exact-xdist elapsed times for the converted tests are RECORDED against the current-fixture baseline' since step 6 already declares timing as evidence only.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add test_hook_fails_when_rebar_build_commit_empty (test_attestation_signing.py:407-424) to the materializer inventory and migrate its inline `git archive HEAD`+`tar -x` full-checkout to the shared minimal fixture, then re-derive the full-tree build-site list via a `git archive` string sweep, not just the two named helpers.
evidence: Plan: 'It supersedes _clean_tree in test_build_provenance.py plus _self_contained_checkout in test_attestation_signing.py at every build-semantics call site. ... No third checkout materializer survives.'

Code: tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py:411-414 `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(_REPO_ROOT), "archive", "HEAD"] ...); subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", str(tree)] ...)` inside test_hook_fails_when_rebar_build_commit_empty — an inline full-checkout materializer not covered by either named helper.
findings.finding: The plan's materializer inventory (supersede `_clean_tree` + `_self_contained_checkout`, 'No third checkout materializer survives') omits a third full-tree materialization site: `test_hook_fails_when_rebar_build_commit_empty` in tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py archives the full Rebar checkout INLINE (`git -C _REPO_ROOT archive HEAD` + `tar -x`, lines 411-414) without using either named helper. It is the very blank-env probe the plan claims to migrate, yet it is not in the enumerated call-site list.
findings.location: Plan step 2 ('It supersedes _clean_tree ... plus _self_contained_checkout ... No third checkout materializer survives') and step 4; ACs 'Hook-semantics fixtures never archive the full Rebar checkout' / 'The blank-env probe requires a nonzero real-build exit.'
scenarios: tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py:407-424 test_hook_fails_when_rebar_build_commit_empty — its inline `git archive HEAD` + `tar -x` at lines 411-414 keeps archiving the full ~42MB Rebar checkout, violating the AC 'Hook-semantics fixtures never archive the full Rebar checkout' and leaving the blank-env probe unmigrated to the shared minimal fixture.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep the tree for `git archive` / inline `tar -x` in the build-semantics tests and enumerate every occurrence; convert the blank-env probe to the shared minimal-package fixture so no hook-semantics test archives the full Rebar checkout.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the timing AC with the RCA by scoping the claimed reduction to per-cell build work (setup/build seconds) rather than end-to-end host wall-clock, which the RCA attributes to uncontrolled host variation.
evidence: RCA: 'This is a bounded contributor, not the cause of multi-minute host variation.'
AC: 'Focused serial plus exact-xdist evidence shows lower elapsed runner work.'
findings.finding: The 'lower elapsed runner work' AC is in tension with the plan's own RCA, which states the per-worker triple-build is 'a bounded contributor, not the cause of multi-minute host variation' — so the change is not expected to move the dominant cost driver, yet an AC asserts a runner-work reduction.
scenarios: Hosted run shows unchanged or worse wall-clock due to host variation while the fixture change genuinely reduced per-cell build work, leaving reviewers unsure whether the AC passed.

findings.checklist_item: State that the shared tiny-package fixture wires the production hatch_build.py as its build hook and declares a src/rebar/_build_info.py force-include target so the sdist ships the baked file that the install-from-sdist/git-fallback preserve probes depend on.
evidence: hatch_build.py line 122: build_data.setdefault("force_include", {})[str(target)] = str(_TARGET) — the sdist ships _build_info.py precisely so the rebuild-from-sdist preserves the baked SHA (precedence step 2)
test_build_provenance.py test_install_from_sdist_preserves_commit and test_attestation_signing.py test_hook_falls_back_to_git_when_env_unset both rely on the sdist carrying _build_info.py

Plan step 3 only says the fixture 'creates a tiny temporary Hatch package... keeps default PEP 517 isolation... never mocks Hatchling' — it does not state the package must wire the production hook AND declare a _build_info.py force-include target
findings.finding: The tiny Hatch fixture package must reproduce the production hatch_build.py force_include of src/rebar/_build_info.py, or the install-from-sdist preserve-existing (step 2) chain that the git-fallback and sdist-preserve probes depend on will break silently.
findings.location: Plan step 3; Test contract card production_path
scenarios: A tiny fixture package that runs the hook but omits the _build_info.py force-include: the sdist ships no baked file, so the git-fallback/sdist-preserve probes pass for the wrong reason or flip to None
findings.suggested_fix: In step 3, require the fixture package's pyproject.toml to reference the repo's hatch_build.py (not a copy) as its custom build hook and include a src/rebar/_build_info.py target under force_include, matching the production packaging so the sdist ships _build_info.py.
